concept: Models of teaching and their originators (Bruner, Suchman, Ausubel, Oliver and Shaver)
must_teach: Concept attainment model is based on Bruner; inquiry training on Suchman; advance organiser on Ausubel; jurisprudential inquiry on Oliver and Shaver.

concept: Basic requirements of teaching: content knowledge plus pedagogy plus knowledge of learners
must_teach: Subject knowledge alone is insufficient; it must be joined to pedagogical skill. Knowing learners' previous knowledge, abilities and interests is equally a requirement of teaching.

concept: Synchronous vs asynchronous online learning
must_teach: Synchronous learning happens at the same time in real time (e.g. live webinar); freedom from a common time defines asynchronous learning.

concept: Bloom's Knowledge category includes knowledge of criteria; level set by verb
must_teach: Bloom's 1956 Knowledge category covers knowledge of specifics, of ways and means (including knowledge of criteria) and of universals. Recalling criteria is Knowledge; using criteria to judge would be Evaluation.

concept: Workshop: participants do practical work and produce a product
must_teach: A workshop is defined by participants' practical work yielding a product, with short expert input. Seminars and symposia centre on presenting and discussing papers; a conference is a larger meeting for exchange.

concept: Morrison's five steps vs Herbartian five steps
must_teach: Morrison: exploration, presentation, assimilation, organisation, recitation. Herbart (formal steps): preparation, presentation, comparison/association, generalisation, application. Only presentation is common; organisation is Morrison's alone.

concept: Stimulus generalisation in classical conditioning
must_teach: Stimulus generalisation: a response conditioned to one stimulus is evoked by similar stimuli. Discrimination is responding only to the original stimulus; response generalisation is one stimulus evoking several similar responses; spontaneous recovery is return of an extinguished response.

concept: Test-retest reliability gives coefficient of stability
must_teach: Test-retest gives coefficient of stability; parallel forms give equivalence; split-half and Kuder-Richardson give internal consistency; parallel forms after an interval give stability and equivalence.

concept: Classifying influences into institution, facilities, environment factors
must_teach: Administrative support and leadership are institution factors; equipment like projectors, labs, libraries are instructional facilities; physical conditions like noise and light and psychological climate are learning environment.

concept: An assessment's function depends on use; can be formative and summative
must_teach: Feedback that guides further learning is a formative use; counting marks toward the final grade is a summative use; one assessment can serve both functions.

concept: Case method presents realistic problem; role play is unscripted
must_teach: A case describes a real or realistic situation for analysis and decision. Role play gives players a situation and role to improvise; a memorised script makes it dramatisation.

concept: Marcia's identity statuses: exploration and commitment
must_teach: Moratorium = exploration without commitment; diffusion = neither; foreclosure = commitment without exploration; achievement = commitment after exploration.

concept: Concrete-to-abstract vs particular-to-general maxims are distinct
must_teach: Concrete to abstract concerns kind of experience (things to ideas); particular to general concerns scope (cases to rule) and is the basis of the inductive method. They are separate maxims.

concept: Projection devices and the material each projects
must_teach: Episcope projects opaque pictures/objects by reflected light; slide projector (diascope) projects small mounted transparent slides; OHP projects large writable transparencies; LCD projector shows computer output.

concept: Motivation theories: Alderfer ERG, Herzberg, Vroom, McClelland
must_teach: Alderfer: existence, relatedness, growth (ERG). Herzberg: hygiene factors and motivators. Vroom: valence, instrumentality, expectancy. McClelland: needs for achievement, affiliation, power.

concept: Self-assessment and peer assessment can be formative without marks
must_teach: Self-assessment is mainly reflection against criteria and need not produce a grade. Peer assessment can be confined to comments to improve drafts, without marks.

concept: Cognitive processes under each category of revised Bloom's taxonomy
must_teach: Remember: recognising, recalling. Understand: interpreting, exemplifying, classifying, summarising, inferring, comparing, explaining. Apply: executing, implementing. Analyse: differentiating, organising, attributing. Metacognitive knowledge includes self-knowledge.

concept: Aptitude-treatment interaction (Cronbach and Snow)
must_teach: Cronbach and Snow's aptitude-treatment interaction: a method's effect depends on its interaction with learner characteristics, so the same method gives different results with different learners; no method is best for all.

concept: Reflective level: learners reach and test generalisations themselves
must_teach: At understanding level the teacher explains generalisations and learners grasp and apply them; at reflective level learners face a problem and arrive at and test generalisations through their own inquiry.

concept: Components of the skill of probing questioning
must_teach: Probing components: prompting (hints after no/wrong answer), seeking further information, refocusing (relating answer to another situation), redirection (same question to other students), increasing critical awareness (asking for justification).

concept: Sequence of steps in educational diagnosis and remediation
must_teach: Diagnosis order: identify students with difficulty, locate specific areas of difficulty, find causes, then plan remedial instruction.

concept: Seligman's learned helplessness
must_teach: Learned helplessness (Seligman): after uncontrollable failure, learners believe outcomes do not depend on their actions and stop trying even when success is possible. Test anxiety is fear interfering during tests; field dependence is a cognitive style; identity diffusion is Marcia's status.

concept: Guilford's divergent vs convergent production
must_teach: Guilford: convergent production seeks one correct answer; divergent production generates many answers and underlies creativity. Unusual-uses tests measure divergent production, scored for fluency, flexibility, originality.

concept: Computing CGPA as credit-weighted average of SGPAs
must_teach: CGPA = sum of (semester credits x SGPA) / total credits; not the simple average of SGPAs. Example: (160+140+60)/50 = 7.2.

concept: Memory level is necessary but insufficient; does not develop critical thought
must_teach: Memory level teaching supplies facts needed for higher levels but does not develop independent critical thinking; that is the outcome of reflective level teaching.

concept: Post-active (reflection) and pre-active (planning) phases
must_teach: Analysing a lesson already taught is post-active (evaluation, reflection); planning the next lesson is pre-active; interactive is classroom delivery. Phases feed into each other cyclically.

concept: National Academic Depository stores degrees and mark-sheets digitally
must_teach: National Academic Depository (accessed through DigiLocker) is an online store of academic awards for verification; Academic Bank of Credits records credits earned; NDLI is a digital library; Shodhganga holds theses.
flag: NEW?: NAD and ABC fit across 4.6 and 6.7; ensure guide names NAD (currently not in outline). Verify current NAD-DigiLocker arrangement.

concept: Constructivism treats errors as information about learners' ideas
must_teach: Constructivism: learners build knowledge by testing existing ideas against experience; errors reveal those ideas and are opportunities for restructuring understanding.

concept: Krathwohl's Responding level and its sub-levels (acquiescence)
must_teach: Affective taxonomy: Receiving, Responding, Valuing, Organisation, Characterisation. Responding sub-levels: acquiescence in responding, willingness to respond, satisfaction in response; compliant action is Responding, mere attention is Receiving.

concept: Morrison's recitation step means oral presentation of mastered unit
must_teach: Recitation is Morrison's fifth and last step; it means the pupil orally presents the mastered unit in own words, not rote reproduction.

concept: Knowles' andragogy assumption: orientation to learning (problem-centred)
must_teach: Knowles' assumptions: self-concept, role of experience, readiness to learn (when social-role tasks demand), orientation to learning (immediate application, problem-centred), motivation (internal), need to know.

concept: Availability of facilities does not ensure use; library as instructional facility
must_teach: Libraries are instructional facilities, but they go unused when teaching does not require independent reading, hours are inconvenient, or students lack library skills; classification does not explain use.

concept: Percentile rank is norm-referenced; percentage of objectives mastered is criterion-referenced
must_teach: Norm-referenced scores locate a student among others (percentile rank); criterion-referenced scores describe mastery of a defined domain (percentage of objectives mastered) without comparison.

concept: Strengths and limits of lecture and demonstration methods
must_teach: Demonstration is more concrete than lecture, but the teacher performs while learners watch, so it gives no hands-on practice. Lecture efficiently transmits information but is not suited to developing skills.

concept: Types of validity: content, concurrent, predictive, construct
must_teach: Content validity: adequate sampling of the course. Concurrent: agreement with a criterion available now. Predictive: forecasting later performance. Construct: reflects the theoretical trait.

concept: Crowder's branching vs Skinner's linear programmed instruction
must_teach: Crowder's branching: larger frames, multiple-choice responses, wrong choices lead to remedial frames (errors used diagnostically). Skinner's linear: small steps, constructed responses, near-errorless learning.

concept: Indian model of micro-teaching vs Stanford model
must_teach: Stanford model used real pupils and videotape feedback. Indian model (Passi/NCERT) uses peers as pupils under simulated conditions and feedback from supervisors and peer observers, without costly equipment; full cycle and one-skill principle retained.

concept: Teaching as a triadic relation
must_teach: Teaching is logically triadic: someone (teacher) teaches something (content) to someone (learner). That teaching is a profession is a separate social fact and does not explain the triadic structure.

concept: Analytic method works from unknown conclusion back to known data
must_teach: Analytic method proceeds from the unknown (conclusion) back to the known (data), showing why each step is taken; synthetic presents proof from data to conclusion; deduction applies a general rule to cases; induction goes from cases to rule.
flag: NEW?: analytic-synthetic method not explicitly in 4.4 list; add to 4.4 or 1.6 (maxim analysis to synthesis).

concept: Test, measurement and evaluation distinguished
must_teach: A test is an instrument; measurement is the process of assigning numbers to performance; evaluation interprets numbers with other evidence and judges worth against objectives.

concept: First levels of Dave, Simpson, Harrow and Krathwohl taxonomies
must_teach: Dave begins with Imitation; Simpson with Perception; Harrow with Reflex movements; Krathwohl (affective) with Receiving.

concept: Relative grading is norm-referenced; absolute grading is criterion-referenced
must_teach: Relative grading awards grades by position in the group (norm-referenced); absolute grading uses fixed pre-set standards (criterion-referenced).

concept: Diorama vs mock-up vs cut-away model
must_teach: Diorama: three-dimensional miniature scene with figures before a painted background. Mock-up: simplified working replica for training. Cut-away model: shows the inside of an object. Specimen: real object or sample.

concept: Integration vs inclusion of learners with disabilities
must_teach: Integration places the learner in the regular setting without changing the system; inclusion requires the institution to change, removing barriers and providing accommodation. Segregation means separate settings; exclusion means denial of education.

concept: Number of SWAYAM National Coordinators (ten per MoE 2026)
must_teach: SWAYAM National Coordinators listed as ten: NPTEL, UGC, AICTE, CEC, IGNOU, IIM Bangalore, NITTTR, INI, NCERT, NIOS; older sources list nine.
flag: DATED: says ten National Coordinators citing MoE March 2026 note on PM e-Vidya (older sources list nine; INI addition) — verify current list and count.

concept: Order of Gagné's nine events of instruction
must_teach: Gagné's events: gaining attention, informing learners of objective, stimulating recall, presenting stimulus, providing guidance, eliciting performance, providing feedback, assessing performance, enhancing retention and transfer.

concept: SWAYAM PRABHA is free DTH broadcast; SWAYAM gives credits
must_teach: SWAYAM PRABHA is one-way DTH television, free on DD Free Dish, needing no internet and offering no assessment. SWAYAM is the interactive MOOC platform with quizzes, exams and credit transfer.

concept: Vygotsky's actual vs potential development levels and ZPD
must_teach: Actual development = independent problem-solving; potential development = problem-solving with guidance from a more capable person; ZPD is the distance between the two.

concept: UGC ten-point grade scale: F and Ab carry zero
must_teach: UGC CBCS ten-point scale: O 10, A+ 9, A 8, B+ 7, B 6, C 5, P 4, F 0, Ab 0. Credits of F/Ab courses count in SGPA denominator.
flag: DOUBT: claim that F/Ab credits still count in SGPA calculation follows the UGC illustration but practice varies by university — verify wording.

concept: Conservation is achieved in concrete operational stage via reversibility
must_teach: Pre-operational children fail conservation tasks; conservation is the chief achievement of the concrete operational stage and depends on understanding reversibility.

concept: Order and meaning of Dave's psychomotor levels
must_teach: Dave's order: imitation, manipulation, precision, articulation, naturalisation. Articulation = coordinating a series of actions harmoniously; copying a model is imitation.

concept: Flipped classroom is one model of blended learning
must_teach: Blended learning combines face-to-face and online learning; the flipped classroom (content online first, class time for application) is one blended model; rotation and flex models are blended but not flipped.

concept: Checklist vs rating scale vs rubric
must_teach: Checklist records presence/absence; rating scale records degree on a numerical or verbal scale; a rubric adds descriptors of performance at each level (analytic per criterion, holistic overall).

concept: Validity ceiling equals square root of reliability (index of reliability)
must_teach: Maximum validity coefficient = square root of reliability coefficient (index of reliability); e.g. reliability 0.64 gives maximum validity 0.80.

concept: Support material vs instructional facilities
must_teach: Support material: aids and resources for particular content (charts, models, handouts, worksheets, slides). Instructional facilities: institutional infrastructure (halls, labs, libraries, networks).

concept: Direct vs indirect assessment tools in outcome-based education
must_teach: Direct assessment examines actual performance (tests, assignments, projects); indirect assessment gathers opinions about learning via surveys (course-exit, alumni, employer). Outcome attainment relies mainly on direct tools.
flag: NEW?: outcome-based education (CO/PO attainment, direct/indirect tools) not in outline; consider adding to 6.3 or 6.9.

concept: Order of bands in Dale's Cone of Experience
must_teach: Dale's cone from base: direct purposeful experiences, contrived experiences, dramatised experiences, demonstrations, study trips, exhibits, television, motion pictures, recordings/radio/still pictures, visual symbols, verbal symbols.

concept: Kohlberg's conventional level: law and order orientation
must_teach: Kohlberg: pre-conventional (punishment, self-interest), conventional (good boy/girl, law and order stage 4), post-conventional (social contract, universal principles that may override rules). Heteronomous is Piaget's term.

concept: Cooperative climate favours learning; competition not always harmful
must_teach: Research favours cooperative over competitive classroom structures for achievement and relationships, but moderate friendly competition (between groups or against one's own record) can motivate.

concept: Reflective level needs a democratic, open classroom
must_teach: Reflective level teaching requires freedom to doubt, question and propose alternatives, so it needs a democratic open climate; an authoritarian classroom denies this.

concept: Limits of academic freedom
must_teach: Academic freedom protects inquiry, expression of evidence-based (even controversial) views, criticism of theories and choice of method, but does not permit disregarding the prescribed curriculum or evaluation norms.

concept: Cumulative record vs portfolio, anecdotal record, sociogram
must_teach: Cumulative record: institution's year-by-year comprehensive record of a student. Portfolio: student's selection of work with reflection. Anecdotal record: single incidents. Sociogram: choices within a group.

concept: Evaluation methods at memory, understanding and reflective levels
must_teach: Memory level: oral and written recall tests. Understanding level: both objective-type and essay-type items. Reflective level: mainly essay-type tests.

concept: Teacher-centred vs learner-centred: roles and choice of approach
must_teach: Learner-centred teaching changes the teacher's role to designer and guide but does not make it unimportant, and uses formative assessment extensively. Teacher-centred exposition suits introducing unfamiliar content; choice depends on objectives, learners and content.

concept: Features of the Herbartian approach
must_teach: Herbartian approach: orderly presentation via formal steps, rests on doctrine of apperception, uses recitation and drill, and is teacher-centred.

concept: Correction for guessing formula S = R - W/(n-1)
must_teach: Correction for guessing: S = R - W/(n-1), n = number of options; omitted items are not counted. E.g. 40 - 12/3 = 36.

concept: Thorndike's law of readiness
must_teach: Law of readiness: when ready, acting satisfies and not acting annoys; when not ready, forced action annoys. Law of effect: consequences after a response; law of exercise: use and disuse.

concept: Kelley's upper and lower 27 per cent groups in item analysis
must_teach: Item analysis uses upper and lower 27 per cent of examinees ranked by total score (Kelley); for 200 examinees each group has 54.

concept: Raw scores need a norm or criterion frame of reference
must_teach: A raw score has little meaning alone; it must be interpreted against a norm (others' performance) or criterion (standard) to become information.

concept: Bandura's four sources of self-efficacy; mastery strongest
must_teach: Bandura's sources of self-efficacy: mastery experiences (strongest), vicarious experiences, verbal persuasion, physiological/emotional states.

concept: Psychological bases of maxims of teaching
must_teach: Known to unknown rests on Herbart's apperception; whole to part on Gestalt perception; simple to complex on graded difficulty; particular to general on inductive reasoning.

concept: Types of tutorial: supervision, group, practical
must_teach: Supervision tutorial: tutor with one or two students on their written work (Oxbridge). Group tutorial: small group clearing common difficulties after lectures. Practical tutorial: skills in lab or workshop.

concept: Bruner's theory of instruction features; discovery for all ages
must_teach: Bruner's theory of instruction (Toward a Theory of Instruction) addresses predisposition to learn, structure of knowledge, sequence and reinforcement. He held any subject can be taught in some honest form to any child, so discovery is not excluded for young children.

concept: Justifying with reasons is Evaluate (cognitive), not Valuing
must_teach: Justifying a choice against criteria is the cognitive process Evaluate; Valuing is affective, concerning attitude and commitment.

concept: Krathwohl's Receiving sub-levels: selected attention
must_teach: Receiving sub-levels: awareness, willingness to receive, controlled or selected attention. Responding begins only when the learner reacts.

concept: Flanders' categories: 8-9 student talk, 10 silence, questions indirect
must_teach: FIACS: categories 1-4 indirect teacher influence (4 = asking questions), 5-7 direct influence, 8-9 student talk, 10 silence/confusion. Only verbal behaviour is coded.

concept: Good teaching aims at learner independence, not dependence
must_teach: Good teaching gives guidance suited to learners' needs so that it can be withdrawn; its aim is an independent learner, not permanent dependence on the teacher.

concept: Knowles' readiness and experience are separate assumptions
must_teach: Knowles: readiness to learn arises from developmental tasks of social roles; adults have a large reservoir of experience as a resource. These are separate assumptions, neither causing the other.

concept: Incident method (Pigors) as variant of case method
must_teach: In the incident method (Paul Pigors) learners get a brief incident and must obtain remaining facts by questioning before analysis; in an ordinary case study full facts are given. In-basket method simulates handling a manager's papers.

concept: Evaluation is integral to teaching; communication a separate feature
must_teach: Evaluation is integral to teaching because the teacher must know whether objectives are achieved to adjust instruction. Teaching being communication is a separate characteristic.

concept: Problem-solving method vs project method
must_teach: Both involve purposeful learner activity, but problem-solving is chiefly mental and ends in a solution, while a project is carried out in a real-life setting and ends in a tangible product.

concept: Specific learning disabilities: dysgraphia, dyslexia, dyscalculia, dyspraxia
must_teach: Dysgraphia = writing difficulty (letter formation, spacing); dyslexia = reading; dyscalculia = number; dyspraxia = planning and coordination of movement.

concept: cMOOCs rest on connectivism (Siemens, Downes)
must_teach: cMOOCs, designed by Siemens and Downes on connectivist lines, have learners find, create and share content; connectivism sees learning as forming connections across networks. xMOOCs are content-delivery courses.

concept: Johnson and Johnson's social interdependence types
must_teach: Negative interdependence (competition): one succeeds only if others fail. Positive interdependence (cooperation): each succeeds only if others succeed. No interdependence (individualistic): results independent.

concept: Facility access is necessary but not sufficient for educational use
must_teach: Providing ICT facilities does not by itself change teaching methods; use depends on teacher skill, willingness, time and institutional support. Access is necessary but not sufficient.

concept: Teaching variables and independent/dependent variables in experiments
must_teach: In analysis of teaching, teacher is independent variable, learner dependent, and content/methods intervening. In an experiment, the manipulated factor (method) is independent and the measured outcome (achievement) is dependent.

concept: Adult experience as resource and possible hindrance
must_teach: Knowles saw experience as adults' richest resource, but it can also produce fixed habits, biases and assumptions that resist new learning, requiring unlearning.

concept: ePathshala (NCERT/CIET) vs e-PG Pathshala (UGC)
must_teach: ePathshala (NCERT's CIET) provides school textbooks and e-resources; e-PG Pathshala is UGC/INFLIBNET e-content for postgraduate courses; Shodhganga holds theses; NPTEL is IIT/IISc engineering content.

concept: Origin of formative/summative: Scriven (curriculum), Bloom (student learning)
must_teach: Scriven (1967) coined formative and summative evaluation for curriculum/programme evaluation; Bloom, Hastings and Madaus (1971) applied them to student learning, especially mastery learning.

concept: CBCS course types: AECC, SEC, DSE, GE
must_teach: UGC CBCS: Core, Discipline Specific Elective, Generic Elective, Ability Enhancement Compulsory Courses (Environmental Science, English/MIL Communication) and Skill Enhancement Courses (skill-based, chosen from a pool).
flag: DATED: uses 2015 UGC CBCS course categories (AECC/SEC/DSE/GE); CCFUP 2022 renamed/reshaped these (AEC, SEC, VAC, MDC) — guide should present both and note which framework the question assumes.

concept: Achievement goal theory: performance vs mastery goals
must_teach: Mastery (learning) goals aim to understand and improve; performance goals aim to demonstrate ability relative to others; work-avoidance aims at minimal effort.

concept: Teaching vs instruction
must_teach: Instruction is organised imparting of knowledge and can be done by a book, programme or machine; teaching in the strict sense involves a person interacting with the learner. All teaching includes instruction, not all instruction is teaching.

concept: Split-half reliability inflated for speed tests
must_teach: Split-half (odd-even) gives spuriously high reliability on speed tests because halves are nearly identical; test-retest or parallel forms should be used for speeded tests. Power tests can use split-half.

concept: Kolb's four learning styles and their mode pairs
must_teach: Diverger: concrete experience + reflective observation; assimilator: abstract conceptualisation + reflective observation; converger: abstract conceptualisation + active experimentation; accommodator: concrete experience + active experimentation.

concept: Motivation at memory (extrinsic) and reflective (intrinsic) levels
must_teach: At memory level motivation is mostly extrinsic (marks, praise, reproof); at reflective level it is mostly intrinsic, from the learner's felt problem.

concept: Enabling vs terminal objectives; Eisner's expressive objectives
must_teach: Terminal objective: what the learner can do at the end. Enabling objectives: intermediate component skills found by task analysis. Expressive objectives (Eisner) describe an encounter without specifying outcome.

concept: Ausubel's progressive differentiation vs integrative reconciliation
must_teach: Progressive differentiation: present most general, inclusive ideas first, then detail. Integrative reconciliation: explicitly relate new ideas to earlier ones and resolve contradictions.

concept: Halo effect vs leniency and central tendency errors
must_teach: Halo effect: favourable impression on one trait spreads to rating of unrelated traits. Leniency error: rating everyone high. Central tendency error: rating everyone near the middle.

concept: Creative Commons licence elements BY, SA, NC, ND
must_teach: BY = attribution required; SA = share-alike (adaptations under same licence); NC = non-commercial; ND = no derivatives. Open licences remove the need for individual permission.

concept: Forum: audience participation after lecture under a chairperson
must_teach: A forum is open discussion where the whole audience asks questions and comments, usually after a lecture, panel or symposium. In panel discussion and symposium, a few selected persons on the platform do the main talking.

concept: Andragogy, heutagogy and the PAH continuum
must_teach: Andragogy involves learners in diagnosing needs; heutagogy (Hase and Kenyon) emphasises capability and double-loop learning with the learner determining the path; pedagogy-andragogy-heutagogy form a continuum of increasing autonomy.

concept: UGC SWAYAM credit transfer regulations
must_teach: UGC (Credit Framework for Online Learning Courses through SWAYAM) Regulations allow institutions to accept SWAYAM courses up to a ceiling per semester and give equivalent credit.
flag: DATED: credit-transfer ceiling (20%/40%) depends on UGC regulations version (2016, 2021) — guide should give the current limit with date.

concept: Fixed cut-off is criterion-referenced; top percentage is norm-referenced
must_teach: A fixed minimum score that any number can meet is criterion-referenced; selection by rank (top x per cent) is norm-referenced; selection tests often combine both.

concept: Formal operational thought is abstract and hypothetical
must_teach: Piaget's formal operational stage frees thought from the concrete: reasoning about propositions, possibilities and hypotheses. Dependence on concrete objects marks the concrete operational stage.

concept: Elaborative vs maintenance rehearsal (Craik and Lockhart)
must_teach: Maintenance rehearsal is plain repetition to hold items in short-term memory; elaborative rehearsal links items to existing knowledge (deep processing, Craik and Lockhart) and aids long-term retention.

concept: Chunking overcomes limited working memory capacity (Miller 7 plus/minus 2)
must_teach: Miller: short-term/working memory holds about seven plus or minus two items; chunking groups items into meaningful units to stay within capacity. Interference explains forgetting; the sensory register is brief.

concept: Mayer's coherence and modality principles of multimedia design
must_teach: Mayer's coherence principle: extraneous material, even attractive, reduces learning. Modality principle: graphics are better with spoken narration than on-screen text.

concept: Gagné's events paired with internal learning processes
must_teach: Gaining attention supports reception; informing objective creates expectancy; learning guidance supports semantic encoding; feedback provides reinforcement.

concept: CAI modes: tutorial, drill-and-practice, simulation; branching resemblance
must_teach: Tutorial mode teaches new material through dialogue and, with remedial routing, resembles Crowder's branching programming. Drill and practice rehearses taught material; simulation models a real system.

concept: Piaget's egocentric speech vs Vygotsky's private speech
must_teach: Piaget saw children's self-talk as egocentric speech showing immaturity that fades; Vygotsky saw it as private speech that guides and regulates thought and later becomes inner speech.

concept: Performance assessment: validity gain, reliability and practicability loss
must_teach: Replacing written tests with observed performance raises validity (direct evidence) but lowers reliability (small sample, observer variation) and practicability (time); rubrics and multiple observations limit the loss.

concept: Cyclic relation of pre-active, interactive and post-active phases
must_teach: Post-active reflection can lead to action research; interactive decisions are steered by learners' verbal and non-verbal feedback; post-active evaluation feeds the next pre-active plan; experience shortens but does not remove planning.

concept: Locating an objective in the revised taxonomy table
must_teach: Taxonomy table: verb gives cognitive process, noun gives knowledge dimension (factual, conceptual, procedural, metacognitive). Judging one's own study strategies = Evaluate x metacognitive knowledge.

concept: Concept attainment model syntax and information-processing family
must_teach: Concept attainment (Bruner) phases: presentation of examples and non-examples, testing attainment, analysis of thinking strategies; it is in the information-processing family, as are inquiry training and advance organiser.

concept: Steps in constructing an achievement test
must_teach: Order: planning with blueprint, writing items, try-out on a sample, item analysis, assembling the final form.

concept: Keller's ARCS model of motivation
must_teach: ARCS: Attention (e.g. puzzling case), Relevance (link to goals), Confidence (graded tasks with early success), Satisfaction (rewards, use of learning).

concept: Features of problem-based learning
must_teach: PBL presents an ill-structured problem before content is taught; the tutor acts as facilitator; a physical product is characteristic of the project method, not PBL.

concept: Converting raw score to z and T-score
Morrison's mastery formula: teach, test, re-teach until mastery
must_teach: Morrison's mastery test ends assimilation; pupils who fall short of the mastery standard return to supervised study with corrective help and are re-tested before organisation and recitation.

concept: Lecture lacks feedback from receivers in communication terms
must_teach: In communication terms a lecture has sender, message, channel and receivers, but largely lacks feedback; questions, pauses and short tasks restore the feedback loop.

concept: Continued relevance of traditional aids in ICT classrooms
must_teach: Traditional aids (charts, models, chalkboard) remain useful: inexpensive, need no electricity, under teacher's control, models can be handled. Good teaching combines traditional and digital support.

concept: Independent, dependent, moderator and intervening variables
must_teach: Manipulated factor is independent; measured outcome is dependent; a moderator changes the strength of the relation; an intervening variable lies on the causal path transmitting the effect.

concept: Computing SGPA from ten-point grade points
must_teach: Grade points: O 10, A+ 9, A 8, B+ 7, B 6, C 5, P 4. With equal credits SGPA is the mean: (10+9+7+4)/4 = 7.5.

concept: Duration of the Indian micro-teaching cycle (36 minutes)
must_teach: Indian micro-teaching cycle: teach 6, feedback 6, re-plan 12, re-teach 6, re-feedback 6 = 36 minutes; 180 minutes allows 5 cycles.

concept: Updating CGPA with a new semester (credit-weighted)
must_teach: CGPA = total credit points / total credits: (80x7.0 + 20x8.5)/100 = 730/100 = 7.3; not the simple average of CGPA and SGPA.

concept: PASS theory of intelligence (Das, Naglieri, Kirby)
must_teach: PASS (Das, Naglieri and Kirby, after Luria): Planning, Attention-arousal, Simultaneous and Successive processing; basis of the Cognitive Assessment System.

concept: Original taxonomy cumulative hierarchy; revised allows overlap
must_teach: Bloom 1956 assumed a strict cumulative hierarchy; Anderson and Krathwohl (2001) kept the order of complexity but allowed categories to overlap (e.g. explaining more complex than executing).

concept: Identifying synchronous vs asynchronous course components
must_teach: Synchronous components require everyone present at the same moment (live lecture); forums, recorded lectures and quizzes open over a time window are asynchronous.

concept: Symposium (prepared statements) vs panel discussion (spontaneous exchange)
must_teach: Symposium: several experts give prepared statements on different aspects one after another. Panel discussion: experts converse spontaneously under a moderator before an audience. Seminar centres on papers; workshop on practical product.

concept: Teaching as communication; noise includes semantic and psychological
must_teach: Teaching fits the communication model: sender, message, channel, receiver, feedback. Noise is anything distorting the message: physical, semantic (unfamiliar terms), psychological (anxiety, prejudice).

concept: Dewey's steps of reflective thinking combine induction and deduction
must_teach: Dewey's five steps: felt difficulty, location/definition, suggested solutions (hypotheses, inductive), reasoning out implications (deductive), testing by observation. Reflection begins in doubt, not fixed premises.

concept: Which digital services need internet: SWAYAM, Virtual Labs vs SWAYAM PRABHA
must_teach: SWAYAM courses and Virtual Labs are web-based and need internet; SWAYAM PRABHA via DTH/DD Free Dish needs no internet at the learner's end.

concept: Inductive conclusions are probable because of the inductive leap
must_teach: Induction moves from limited particular instances to a general rule; the conclusion goes beyond the evidence, so it is probable, whereas valid deduction yields certainty.

concept: Vygotsky: social origin of higher mental functions
must_teach: Vygotsky held that higher mental functions appear first between people (social plane) and then within the individual; hence classroom dialogue is central.

concept: Standard deviation shows spread; implication for differentiation
must_teach: Mean shows general level, standard deviation shows spread; with equal means, the class with larger SD is more heterogeneous and needs more differentiated instruction.

concept: NEP 2020 teacher provisions: CPD and four-year integrated B.Ed.
must_teach: NEP 2020 expects continuous professional development for teachers (50 hours a year) and sets the four-year integrated B.Ed. as minimum qualification for school teachers by 2030; these are separate provisions.
flag: NEW?: NEP 2020 teacher-education provisions not explicit in outline; place in 1.10 or 1.8.

concept: Computing course outcome attainment percentage
must_teach: Outcome attainment = proportion of students reaching the set level: 52/80 = 65 per cent, compared with the target (60 per cent) to judge attainment.
flag: NEW?: OBE attainment calculation not in outline; add under 6.3 or 6.9.

concept: Normal curve: about 68 per cent within one SD
must_teach: In a normal distribution about 34 per cent lie between mean and 1 SD on each side, so about 68 per cent within plus/minus 1 SD and about 95 per cent within plus/minus 2 SD. IQ mean 100, SD 15.

concept: Trump Plan time shares in team teaching
must_teach: J. Lloyd Trump plan: about 40 per cent large-group instruction, 20 per cent small-group discussion, 40 per cent independent study; teachers work as a team by strengths.

concept: Dewey and Kolb experiential learning; Honey and Mumford styles
must_teach: Kolb built his cycle on Dewey, Lewin and Piaget with reflection on experience central. Honey and Mumford: activist-concrete experience, reflector-reflective observation, theorist-abstract conceptualisation, pragmatist-active experimentation.

concept: Computing facility value and discrimination index
must_teach: Facility value = (RU + RL)/(NU + NL); discrimination index = (RU - RL)/N of one group. E.g. 33/60 = 0.55 and 15/30 = 0.50.

concept: Retention and forgetting: distributed practice, overlearning, Ebbinghaus
must_teach: Meaningful material is retained better than nonsense material; distributed practice beats massed practice; overlearning improves retention; Ebbinghaus's curve shows forgetting fastest soon after learning.

concept: Projected vs non-projected aids
must_teach: Projected aids are thrown on a screen by a projector: slides, filmstrips, transparencies, films, opaque projection. Non-projected: flash cards, charts, flannel boards, models, bulletin boards.

concept: Divergent, higher-order questions vs convergent questions
must_teach: Convergent questions have one correct answer (recall or computation); divergent questions have many acceptable answers and call for prediction, imagination and reasoning, typically higher-order.

concept: NEP 2020 assessment reform direction
must_teach: NEP 2020 shifts assessment from summative testing of rote memory to regular, formative, competency-based assessment testing higher-order skills, with holistic progress reporting.

concept: Classifying objectives across cognitive, affective, psychomotor domains
must_teach: Effortless automatic skill = psychomotor Naturalisation (Dave); holding to a value under pressure = affective Valuing; designing an original product = cognitive Create; stating steps = cognitive Remember.

concept: Interpretive exercise vs cloze procedure
must_teach: Interpretive exercise: introductory material (passage, table, graph) followed by several objective items testing interpretation and inference. Cloze test deletes words at intervals to measure reading comprehension.

concept: Diagnostic tests: many items per sub-skill; not for grading
must_teach: Diagnostic tests contain many items per narrow sub-skill to identify error patterns reliably; separately, they are generally not used for grading.

concept: Percentile normalisation across CBT shifts assumes comparable ability
must_teach: Multi-shift CBTs report within-shift percentiles; comparing them across shifts assumes candidates of similar ability are distributed across shifts (random allotment); papers differ, so raw scores cannot be compared.

concept: NAAC's Internal Quality Assurance Cell (IQAC)
must_teach: NAAC recommends each institution set up an IQAC to plan, guide and monitor quality; it develops benchmarks, collects stakeholder feedback and prepares the AQAR. Academic Council approves courses and regulations; Board of Studies handles subject syllabi.

concept: NEP 2020 multiple entry-exit awards by year
must_teach: Four-year UG under NEP 2020/CCFUP: certificate after 1 year, diploma after 2, bachelor's degree after 3, honours or honours with research after 4; credits held in the Academic Bank of Credits for re-entry.

concept: MOOC completion rate depends on the base used
must_teach: MOOC completion rate on enrolments = completers/enrolments (1,500/20,000 = 7.5 per cent); on starters it is 1,500/6,000 = 25 per cent; the base must be stated.

concept: Understanding level depends on memory and prepares for reflective
must_teach: The levels form a ladder: understanding level requires memory level as prerequisite and prepares the ground for reflective level.

concept: RPwD Act 2016: 5 per cent reservation in higher education
must_teach: RPwD Act 2016 requires government and government-aided higher education institutions to reserve not less than 5 per cent seats for persons with benchmark disabilities, with 5 years upper age relaxation; 4 per cent applies to government employment.

concept: Scaling marks of different examiners via standard scores
must_teach: When examiners differ in mean and SD, raw marks should be converted to standard scores (z or T) before combining; otherwise the examiner with larger spread dominates. This is scaling or moderation.

concept: Bandura: learning without reinforcement; acquisition vs performance
must_teach: Bandura showed behaviour is acquired by observing a model without reinforcement; reinforcement (direct or vicarious) mainly affects performance of the acquired behaviour.

concept: Higher-order vs lower-order levels in revised Bloom's taxonomy
must_teach: Remember, Understand and Apply are lower-order; Analyse, Evaluate and Create are higher-order. Percentage of higher-order items = their count over total.
flag: DOUBT: some sources (and HOTS lists) treat Apply as higher-order; question defines the convention in its stem, so answer is safe, but guide should note the varying convention.

concept: Mnemonics impose artificial organisation as retrieval cues
must_teach: Mnemonic devices (acronyms, rhymes, images) aid retention of unrelated facts by imposing artificial organisation that supplies retrieval cues.

concept: Biggs' constructive alignment of outcomes, teaching and assessment
must_teach: John Biggs's constructive alignment requires teaching activities and assessment tasks to call for the same performance as the intended learning outcome; mismatch is a failure of alignment, not of reliability or predictive validity.

concept: Academic Bank of Credits function
must_teach: The Academic Bank of Credits stores credits from recognised institutions in a student's account for transfer and redemption toward certificate, diploma or degree, supporting multiple entry and exit; the National Academic Depository stores awards.

concept: Training, teaching and indoctrination distinguished
must_teach: Training: repeated practice of a specific skill to a standard. Teaching: explanation with reasons engaging understanding and objections. Indoctrination: beliefs presented as beyond question. Conditioning: stimulus-response association without reason.

concept: Fair individual marks in group projects: group mark plus peer ratings
must_teach: Fair group-project marking combines a mark for the group product with peer ratings of each member's contribution against agreed criteria, to reward contribution and discourage free riding.

concept: Conference vs seminar
must_teach: A conference is a large gathering on a broad theme with plenary lectures and parallel sessions where papers are presented; a seminar is smaller and narrower; both include paper presentation.

concept: Features of the reflective level (Hunt's model)
must_teach: Reflective level: teacher poses problems creating cognitive conflict; no source including textbook is final authority; evaluation covers attitudes, involvement and critical ability; learners' level of aspiration must be reasonably high.

concept: Rewards and intrinsic motivation (Deci and Ryan, self-determination theory)
must_teach: Informational unexpected praise sustains intrinsic motivation; expected tangible rewards for interesting tasks can undermine it; autonomy support promotes it; extrinsic motivation is useful for uninteresting tasks and is not always harmful.

concept: Bloom's original taxonomy runs simple to complex
must_teach: Bloom 1956 order: Knowledge, Comprehension, Application, Analysis, Synthesis, Evaluation, simple to complex, each building on those below; Comprehension is prerequisite to Application.

concept: Simulation for skills and decisions; debriefing essential
must_teach: Simulation is used mainly for skills, decisions and attitudes costly or risky to practise in reality (flying, surgery, teaching); debriefing afterwards analyses the experience and turns it into learning.

concept: Institution-related factors: class size, assessment policy, faculty development
must_teach: Institution-related factors (in all institutions, public or private) include class size and teacher-student ratio, assessment policy that encourages or discourages innovation, and faculty development opportunities.

concept: Spearman-Brown prophecy formula for split-half reliability
must_teach: Full-test reliability = 2r/(1 + r) where r is half-test correlation; e.g. 1.20/1.60 = 0.75. Longer tests are more reliable.

concept: Slavin: group goals plus individual accountability
must_teach: Slavin found cooperative learning raises achievement when there are group goals/rewards and individual accountability (team success depends on each member's learning); group-only assessment invites free riding.

concept: Elements of a model of teaching (Joyce and Weil)
must_teach: Joyce and Weil describe models by focus (central aim), syntax (sequence of phases), social system (roles and relationships), principles of reaction, and support system (special materials and facilities).

concept: Choosing workshop, symposium or seminar by purpose
must_teach: Workshop: skill training producing a product. Symposium: successive expert presentations on aspects of a theme before an audience. Seminar: in-depth discussion and critique of a paper.

concept: INFLIBNET services: Shodhganga, ShodhShuddhi, Vidwan, IRINS
must_teach: Shodhganga: repository of Indian doctoral theses. ShodhShuddhi: access to plagiarism-detection software. Vidwan: national database of expert profiles. IRINS: institutional research information management system.

concept: Aptitude-treatment interaction with equal overall means
must_teach: When anxious students do better with structured teaching and less anxious with unstructured, with equal overall means, method and learner trait interact (ATI); no method is best for all.

concept: Criterion-referenced cut-offs (Angoff) and score distribution
must_teach: Criterion-referenced cut-offs can be set by expert judgement of minimal competence (e.g. Angoff method); a rank-based quota fixes the success proportion in advance; criterion-referenced scores need not be normal and are often skewed high after effective teaching.

concept: Physical noise as communication barrier reduces learning
must_teach: Excessive noise is a physical-environment factor; in communication terms it is a barrier that distorts or blocks reception of the teacher's message and diverts attention.

concept: Reflective level parallels the scientific method
must_teach: Reflective level teaching moves from felt problem through hypotheses and testing to conclusion, paralleling the scientific method (Dewey); Herbartian steps organise teacher presentation at memory level.

concept: Deductive syllogism gives certain conclusion if premises true
must_teach: Deduction applies a general premise to a particular case; with true premises and valid form the conclusion is certain. Induction goes from observed cases to a general law and is probable; abduction infers best explanation; analogy argues from resemblance.

concept: Bruner's enactive, iconic, symbolic modes and CPA sequence
must_teach: Bruner's modes of representation: enactive (action/objects), iconic (images/pictures), symbolic (language/notation); the concrete-pictorial-abstract sequence follows this order.

concept: Objectives of teaching in higher education beyond transmission
must_teach: Teaching in higher education aims not only at transmitting knowledge but at developing critical thinking, inquiry, judgement, research orientation, values and capacity to create new knowledge.

concept: Order of Harrow's psychomotor taxonomy
must_teach: Harrow: reflex movements, basic fundamental movements, perceptual abilities, physical abilities, skilled movements, non-discursive communication.

concept: Pass percentage as flawed measure of teacher effectiveness
must_teach: Pass percentage is a product measure; student outcomes also depend on entry level, motivation, class size and facilities beyond the teacher's control, so value-added or contextualised measures are fairer.

concept: Ausubel's rote/meaningful x reception/discovery classification
must_teach: Ausubel crossed reception vs discovery (how content becomes available) with rote vs meaningful (how it is incorporated). Discovery without understanding is rote discovery learning.

concept: Diagnosing systematic errors and planning remediation
must_teach: A consistent wrong procedure across items (e.g. subtracting smaller digit from larger in each column) indicates a systematic misconception (regrouping), not carelessness; remedy is re-teaching with concrete material.

concept: Messick: construct under-representation vs construct-irrelevant variance
must_teach: Construct under-representation: test too narrow, omitting important parts of the construct. Construct-irrelevant variance: scores affected by factors outside the construct (e.g. reading speed).

concept: Averaging grade points assumes an interval scale
must_teach: Averaging requires equal units (interval scale); letter grades are strictly ordinal, so computing SGPA treats grade points as equal steps by convention. Nominal names categories; ratio has a true zero.

concept: Characteristics of self-learning materials in ODL
must_teach: Self-learning materials are self-explanatory, self-contained, self-directed, self-motivating and self-evaluating; in-text check-your-progress questions with answers serve self-evaluation.
flag: NEW?: open and distance learning self-learning materials not in outline; add to 4.5 or 5.4.

concept: Accessible digital content: alt text and captions
must_teach: Alternative text on images is read by screen readers for learners with visual impairment; captions on videos serve learners with hearing impairment.

concept: Blended learning extends learning time; flipped is one model
must_teach: Blended learning extends learning time because online activities can be done outside the timetable; the flipped classroom is one blended model, but that classification does not explain the extension.

concept: Identity formation (Erikson, Marcia) vs Kohlberg's moral stages
must_teach: Identity formation (Erikson, Marcia) continues into the early twenties among university students; Kohlberg's stages concern moral reasoning, a separate aspect of development.

concept: Immediate reinforcement and variable-ratio schedule
must_teach: Points given at once after correct responses are immediate positive reinforcement; rewards after an unpredictable number of responses form a variable-ratio schedule producing persistent responding. Negative reinforcement removes something unpleasant; fixed-interval rewards after set time.

concept: Computing teacher talk percentage in FIACS
must_teach: Teacher talk = categories 1-7 (indirect 1-4 plus direct 5-7); student talk 8-9; silence/confusion 10. Teacher talk % = (1-7 tallies)/total x 100, e.g. 450/600 = 75 per cent.

concept: NEP 2020 pedagogy: learner-centred, inquiry-driven, discussion-based
must_teach: NEP 2020 calls for experiential, holistic, integrated, inquiry-driven, discovery-oriented, learner-centred, discussion-based and flexible pedagogy with less rote learning.

concept: Retention percentages on Dale's cone are spurious
must_teach: Dale's cone ranks experiences by abstraction and carried no numbers; popular retention percentages (10% read, 20% heard...) were added by others and lack research support.

concept: NEP 2020 National Educational Technology Forum (NETF)
must_teach: NEP 2020 proposes the National Educational Technology Forum as an autonomous body for free exchange of ideas on use of technology in learning, assessment, planning and administration; National Research Foundation funds research; NTA conducts tests.

concept: Chickering and Gamson's seven principles of good practice
must_teach: Seven principles: student-faculty contact, cooperation among students, active learning, prompt feedback, time on task, high expectations, respect for diverse talents and ways of learning.

concept: Characterisation level and its assessment by sustained observation
must_teach: Characterisation by a value is the highest affective level: consistent habitual conduct; it is judged by conduct observed over time, not single questionnaires or written tests.

concept: Ratio IQ vs deviation IQ (Wechsler)
must_teach: Ratio IQ = MA/CA x 100 fails for adults because mental age levels off in late teens; Wechsler's deviation IQ expresses standing among same-age peers with mean 100, SD 15.

concept: Particular-to-general is induction; general-to-particular deduction also used
must_teach: Particular to general corresponds to induction; general to particular (deduction) is equally used in teaching for practice, verification and problem-solving; good teaching combines induction then deduction.

concept: Gift (honorary) authorship vs ghost authorship
must_teach: Gift/honorary authorship lists a non-contributor as author; ghost authorship omits a real contributor; salami slicing splits one study into many papers; self-plagiarism reuses one's own published work without citation.
flag: SCOPE: research/publication ethics is Unit II material; 1.10 must explicitly cover authorship ethics if this item stays in Unit I.

concept: Serial position effect (primacy and recency)
must_teach: Serial position effect: better recall of first (primacy) and last (recency) items, worst for middle. Von Restorff: distinctive item recalled better; Zeigarnik: unfinished tasks recalled better; Hawthorne: change due to being observed.

concept: Vygotsky's illustration: equal actual level, different ZPD
must_teach: Two children with the same actual development can have different zones (e.g. one year vs four years); instruction should target the zone, so they need different teaching; unaided tests hide the difference.

concept: Purposes of teaching skills: probing, illustrating, stimulus variation, closure
must_teach: Probing deepens a student's response; illustrating with examples clarifies abstract ideas; stimulus variation sustains attention; closure consolidates learning at the end.

concept: Washback (backwash) of testing on teaching
must_teach: Washback is the effect of a test on teaching and learning: negative when it narrows the curriculum (drilling MCQ technique), positive when it encourages desirable learning. Practice effect is score gain from retaking.

concept: Educational measurement is indirect and contains error
must_teach: Learning is inferred from performance on a sample of tasks, so measurement is indirect; sampling, examinee condition and scoring introduce error; obtained score = true score + error, hence reliability and standard error of measurement.

concept: Finding grade needed for a target SGPA
must_teach: With equal credits SGPA is the mean of grade points; target 7.0 over 4 courses needs 28 points; 28 - 19 = 9 = A+. Ten-point scale: O 10, A+ 9, A 8, B+ 7, B 6, C 5, P 4.

concept: SWAYAM features: open enrolment, school to PG, proctored exams, PM e-Vidya
must_teach: SWAYAM has no age bar for enrolment, covers school to postgraduate courses, requires proctored exams for certificates, and is a component of PM e-Vidya.

concept: Action research cycle: plan, act, observe, reflect (Lewin)
must_teach: Action research (Kurt Lewin) follows a spiral of plan, act, observe, reflect to improve practice in one's own setting; ex post facto studies effects after the event without intervention; experiments use control groups and aim at generalisation.
flag: NEW?: action research not in outline; could sit in 1.2 (post-active) or 4.4.

concept: Behavioural objectives state learner's observable behaviour
must_teach: Behavioural objectives specify observable learner performance (Mager), which makes evaluation easier; statements of teacher activities are not objectives.

concept: LMS automates routine tasks but does not replace the teacher
must_teach: An LMS automates distribution of material and scoring of objective quizzes, freeing the teacher for design, qualitative feedback, discussion and individual support; it does not remove the need for a teacher.

concept: Expected chance score from blind guessing
must_teach: Expected chance score = number of items x 1/number of options; 50 items with four options gives 12.5.

concept: Connectivism principles (Siemens, Downes)
must_teach: Connectivism (Siemens and Downes) sees learning as creating and navigating networks of people, sources and devices; learning may reside in non-human appliances; capacity to know more matters more than what is known. Underlies cMOOCs.

concept: Concept of teaching: intentional, task vs achievement sense, Scheffler
must_teach: Teaching is intentional and presupposes a learner; in the task sense it need not result in learning (only the achievement sense implies learning); Scheffler: teaching respects learner's independent judgement, unlike indoctrination.

concept: Computing a weighted rubric score
must_teach: Weighted rubric score = sum of (weight x criterion score); 0.4x4 + 0.3x2 + 0.3x2 = 2.8 of 4 = 70 per cent; unweighted mean ignores weights.

concept: Vroom's motivational force is a product of E x I x V
must_teach: Vroom: motivational force = expectancy x instrumentality x valence; terms multiply, so any zero term makes motivation zero.

concept: Gagné's learning hierarchy: rules require prerequisite concepts
must_teach: Gagné's hierarchy: rule learning requires mastery of component concepts; problem solving lies above rules. Task analysis works downward from the target skill to prerequisites.

concept: Hypotheses in reflective teaching; value of refuted hypotheses
must_teach: A hypothesis is a tentative solution to be tested; a refuted hypothesis still eliminates a possibility, sharpens the problem and trains reasoning from evidence.

concept: Self-pacing principle of programmed instruction
must_teach: Programmed instruction principles include small steps, active responding, immediate feedback (knowledge of results) and self-pacing; a pace fixed for the whole class marks conventional teaching.

concept: Random assignment equalises extraneous variables
must_teach: In experiments comparing methods, random assignment spreads extraneous learner variables (intelligence, motivation, background) evenly so that outcome differences can be attributed to the method.
flag: SCOPE: research-design content (Unit II); map to 1.2 teaching variables only if guide covers experimental control briefly.

concept: Teacher immediacy (Mehrabian)
must_teach: Teacher immediacy (Mehrabian): verbal and non-verbal behaviours (smiling, eye contact, names, moving among students) reducing psychological distance; clarity is intelligibility of explanation; credibility is perceived competence and trustworthiness; efficacy is belief in one's capability.

concept: Effective supervisory feedback in micro-teaching is specific
must_teach: Useful feedback is specific, descriptive, tied to the skill practised and points to a concrete next step; general praise or blame gives nothing to act on.

concept: Peer tutoring benefits tutor; tutorials supplement lectures
must_teach: Peer tutoring benefits the tutor too, since explaining deepens understanding; tutorials supplement lectures by addressing individual difficulties, not replace them.

concept: SGPA change after clearing a failed course
must_teach: SGPA = sum(credits x grade points)/total credits, with F counted as 0 over its credits; replacing F (0) with C (5) in a 4-credit course adds 20 credit points over 20 credits = +1.0.
flag: DOUBT: assumes the cleared grade replaces F in the same semester's SGPA; universities differ on whether supplementary results revise the original SGPA — verify convention.

concept: Maslow's relative satisfaction; McClelland's acquired needs
must_teach: Maslow: lower needs must be reasonably (not completely) satisfied before higher needs emerge. McClelland's acquired-needs theory: achievement, affiliation, power are learned, so achievement motivation can be trained.

concept: Basic requirements of effective teaching
must_teach: Basic requirements include content mastery, knowledge of learners' psychology and communication skill; a belief that ability is fixed lowers expectations and is not a requirement.

concept: NHEQF levels 4.5 to 8; doctorate at level 8
must_teach: NHEQF (UGC) levels 4.5-8: 4.5 UG certificate, 5 UG diploma, 5.5 bachelor's, 6 bachelor's honours/research (4-year), 6.5 master's, 7 master's after 4-year UG/1-year, 8 doctorate.
flag: DOUBT: explanation places master's at 6.5 only; NHEQF also places some master's (e.g. after 4-year UG / M.Tech) at level 7 — verify level table before teaching.

concept: Moore's transactional distance: structure, dialogue, autonomy
must_teach: Moore: transactional distance is psychological and depends on dialogue, structure and learner autonomy; high structure with low dialogue gives greatest distance; more dialogue reduces it.

concept: Stufflebeam's CIPP model of programme evaluation
must_teach: CIPP (Daniel Stufflebeam): Context (needs, goals), Input (resources, plans), Process (implementation), Product (outcomes); decision-oriented programme evaluation.
flag: NEW?: programme evaluation models (CIPP) not in outline; add to 6.1 or 6.3.

concept: SWAYAM PRABHA as one-way mass communication
must_teach: SWAYAM PRABHA telecasts reach a large, dispersed audience through a mass medium with no return channel, so they are one-way mass communication; interaction comes via web portal or SWAYAM.

concept: Portfolio assessment: low inter-rater reliability; rubrics and moderation
must_teach: Portfolios are strong in authenticity and showing growth but weak in inter-rater agreement; remedies are clear rubrics, rater training, double marking and moderation.

concept: Symposium gives many-sided view through multiple speakers
must_teach: A symposium's many-sided view comes from several speakers each treating a different aspect; a closing question session is customary but not the source of breadth.

concept: Indoctrination defined by method and intention, not content
must_teach: Indoctrination implants beliefs to be held regardless of evidence; it is marked by manner and aim, not subject matter. Any content can be taught with reasons or indoctrinated without them.

concept: Ordering tasks by revised Bloom levels (define, explain, compute, design)
must_teach: Define = Remember; explain why = Understand; compute using a known procedure = Apply; design = Create. Ascending: Remember, Understand, Apply, Analyse, Evaluate, Create.

concept: Too many aids overload working memory (cognitive load theory)
must_teach: Cognitive load theory: working memory handles few elements at once; excessive aids or stimuli overload it and divert attention from the objective, hindering learning.

concept: Adult learning thinkers: Knowles, Mezirow, Freire, Hase and Kenyon
must_teach: Knowles: andragogy assumptions about self-directing adults. Mezirow: perspective transformation (transformative learning). Freire: critique of banking education, dialogue. Hase and Kenyon: heutagogy, self-determined learning.

concept: Comment-only feedback improves learning (Butler; Black and Wiliam)
must_teach: Ruth Butler found comments without grades improved learning most; adding grades cancelled the benefit as students attended to the grade. Black and Wiliam recommended comment-only marking.

concept: Moving learners from memory to understanding level
must_teach: Understanding level requires seeing the concept at work in familiar cases and expressing it in one's own words; repetition keeps learners at memory level; open research problems belong to reflective level, which presupposes understanding.

concept: Threaded discussion forum as asynchronous seminar
must_teach: A threaded discussion forum supports extended reasoned discussion over days without simultaneous presence (asynchronous); a webinar is synchronous; podcasts and broadcast e-mail are one-way.

concept: Distractor analysis: non-functional distractors under 5 per cent
must_teach: A distractor chosen by fewer than 5 per cent of examinees is non-functional; a distractor chosen more than the key is over-attractive and should be checked for ambiguity.

concept: Later critiques of Piaget's theory
must_teach: Critiques: Piaget underestimated young children; gave less weight to social-cultural influence than Vygotsky; stage ages vary with culture and schooling (not fixed); not all adults use formal operations in all fields.

concept: Flannel board allows step-by-step build-up via adhesive cut-outs
must_teach: A flannel board lets cut-outs backed with rough material stick, be added, moved or removed, so displays build up step by step; it is a non-projected aid, but that classification does not explain this advantage.

concept: Arnett's emerging adulthood (18-25)
must_teach: Jeffrey Arnett (2000) proposed emerging adulthood (about 18-25) marked by identity exploration, instability and feeling in-between. Erikson: identity crisis; Marcia: identity statuses; Levinson: seasons of adult life.

concept: Kolb's styles are relatively stable preferences, not fixed traits
must_teach: Kolb derived four styles from preferences for stages of the experiential cycle; they are relatively stable but can change with personality, education and career; mature learners integrate all modes.

concept: Restriction of range lowers reliability coefficient
must_teach: Reliability coefficients depend on score spread; in a homogeneous group true variance is small, so error forms a larger share and the coefficient falls (restriction of range).

concept: Correlation does not imply causation; shared variance r squared
must_teach: A correlation of +0.60 shows a moderately strong positive relation but not causation; shared variance is r squared (0.36), not 0.60.

concept: Choosing an aid by objective and class size
must_teach: Aid choice depends on objective and audience: showing motion to a large class needs a projected animation; specimens, charts and flash cards are static and small.

concept: Understanding level uses objective and essay tests
must_teach: Understanding level evaluation uses both essay-type and objective-type tests because understanding is shown through explanation and application as well as recognition; it is more thoughtful than memory level, but that does not explain the test choice.

concept: Matching method to objective and class size: lecture vs demonstration plus practice
must_teach: Lecture suits giving an overview to a large group quickly; manipulative skills require demonstration followed by individual laboratory practice with feedback.

concept: Classifying teacher acts into pre-active, interactive, post-active
must_teach: Preparing questions at home is pre-active; asking them in class to diagnose is interactive; analysing scripts and revising notes afterwards is post-active. Phase is decided by when and why an act is done.

concept: Highest levels of Dave (naturalisation) and Simpson (origination)
must_teach: Dave's five levels end with naturalisation (automatic skill); Simpson's seven levels (perception, set, guided response, mechanism, complex overt response, adaptation, origination) end with origination.
